problem.title: Design a 500K-RPS Priority-Aware Load Shedding Gateway with CoDel & Little's Law
problem.tagline: Keeping P0 checkout at 100% goodput and <15 ms p99 during 3x traffic spikes by shedding P2/P3 work proactively.
problem.purpose: Design an API edge gateway that prevents metastable retry storms, enforces criticality tiers (P0–P3), and adapts concurrency limits dynamically without manual threshold tuning.
problem.prompt: Design a distributed API Gateway handling 500K RPS normal / 1.5M RPS burst across 4 criticality tiers (P0 Checkout/Auth, P1 Core Reads, P2 Analytics, P3 Background), keeping P0/P1 p99 <15 ms and preventing downstream collapse during 5x database slowdowns.

prerequisites.title: CoDel Sojourn-Time Load Shedding
prerequisites.summary: Know how `target = 5 ms` / `interval = 100 ms` detects standing queues and sheds stale requests.

prerequisites.title: Adaptive Concurrency Limiting (Gradient2)
prerequisites.summary: Understand how Little's Law (`L = lambda * W`) dynamically adjusts in-flight concurrency limits from `RTT_min` vs. `RTT_sample`.

spark.summary: Combine a Deficit Round-Robin + CoDel priority scheduler with Little's Law adaptive concurrency limits so P3/P2 traffic sheds with 503 + Retry-After before P0/P1 queues back up.
spark.keyTakeaway: When designing a high-RPS gateway that must protect critical flows during overload, pair priority-tiered CoDel queues with Little's Law adaptive concurrency limits and explicit 503 Retry-After budgets so retry storms never overwhelm downstream pools.
spark.byteSummary:
At 500K RPS bursting to 1.5M RPS, treating `POST /checkout` (P0) identically to `POST /analytics/event` (P3) guarantees that an analytics spike or DB slowdown takes down revenue-critical checkout. Worse, naive HTTP 503s trigger immediate client retries that turn a 3x burst into a 10x metastable retry storm.

The gateway solves this in three coordinated stages: (1) Every incoming request is tagged at the edge with a criticality tier (`P0`–`P3`) and routed into per-tier CoDel queues scheduled via weighted Deficit Round-Robin; (2) An Adaptive Concurrency Controller (Gradient2) continuously compares baseline `RTT_min` against current `RTT_ema` to shrink the global in-flight concurrency limit `L` the moment downstream latency climbs; (3) When `L` is saturated or CoDel sojourn exceeds target, the gateway sheds lowest-priority tiers first (`P3` -> `P2`) with `HTTP 503` + jittered `Retry-After` headers and client-side retry budgets.

Downstream services stay strictly within their healthy Little's Law operating point—preserving 100% goodput and <15 ms p99 for P0/P1 even during severe 5x backend degradations.

learningJourney.title: R & E · Requirements, Little's Law & Overload Math
learningJourney.whyThisMatters: Shows exact concurrency math for 500K RPS and why unbounded queues trigger metastable collapse.

explanation.foundation: By Little's Law (`L = lambda * W`), 500,000 req/s with a healthy 10 ms downstream service time holds `L = 500,000 * 0.010 = 5,000` concurrent in-flight requests across the gateway fleet.
explanation.core: Illustrative Sizing: Suppose 100 gateway pods handle 5,000 RPS each (`L = 50` in-flight/pod). If a downstream DB slows 5x (`W = 50 ms`) while traffic bursts 3x (`1.5M RPS`), unthrottled concurrency would jump to `L = 1,500,000 * 0.050 = 75,000` (15x overload!). By capping per-pod concurrency dynamically at `~50–65` and shedding `P3` (30% of traffic) + `P2` (25% of traffic) early, P0/P1 (`45%` of traffic) stays inside the healthy capacity envelope.
explanation.deepDive: If clients retry 3x immediately on `503`, a 1.5M RPS spike becomes 4.5M RPS of ingress TLS/header parsing. Returning `Retry-After` + enforcing a 10% client retry-budget token bucket prevents retry amplification from saturating gateway CPUs.

learningJourney.title: S · Policy & Priority Tier Classification
learningJourney.whyThisMatters: Defines how criticality tags (`P0`–`P3`) are assigned safely without trusting untrusted client headers.

explanation.foundation: Never trust a client-supplied `X-Priority: P0` header—every caller would mark their traffic P0!
explanation.core: The edge gateway derives criticality deterministically from route + authenticated tenant tier: e.g., `POST /v1/checkout` & `/v1/auth` -> `P0`; `GET /v1/catalog` -> `P1`; `POST /v1/telemetry` -> `P2`; `POST /v1/export` -> `P3`. Each gateway pod maintains 4 lock-free ring queues (`Q0..Q3`) with independent CoDel sojourn timers.
explanation.deepDive: To avoid CPU starvation on `P2/P3` during normal load while protecting `P0` under overload, use weighted Deficit Round-Robin (weights e.g. `8:4:2:1`) combined with global Gradient2 concurrency permits.

sectionDiagram.title: Route Classifier -> P0..P3 CoDel Queues -> Gradient2 Permit Pool

learningJourney.title: H & A · Gateway Data Plane & Adaptive Concurrency
learningJourney.whyThisMatters: Traces how Gradient2 + CoDel coordinate admission without centralized coordination.

explanation.foundation: Each gateway pod runs its own local Gradient2 + CoDel controller—zero cross-pod Redis round-trips on the hot path!
explanation.core: When a request arrives, the pod checks `in_flight < limit`. If `limit` is reached, it immediately sheds the lowest-priority queued item (`P3`, then `P2`) rather than dropping an incoming `P0`! As downstream responses return, Gradient2 updates `limit_new = limit * (RTT_min / RTT_sample) + queue_allowance`, automatically shrinking `limit` during DB slowdowns.
explanation.deepDive: For `P0` requests, reserve a non-preemptible floor (e.g., 30% of `limit`) that `P1–P3` can borrow when `P0` is idle, but `P0` can always reclaim by shedding queued `P2/P3` work.

sectionDiagram.title: Edge Classify -> Priority CoDel -> Gradient2 Permit -> Upstream / 503

learningJourney.title: D · Detailed Design: Anti-Retry-Storm & Edge Shedding
learningJourney.whyThisMatters: Prevents rejected 503 traffic from looping back as a 10x retry storm.

explanation.foundation: Shedding a request at the gateway only saves downstream CPU—if 500K clients retry immediately, the gateway itself still spends CPU on TLS and routing.
explanation.core: Three defenses stop retry storms: (1) Return `HTTP 503` with a jittered `Retry-After` header (e.g., `2–5s` for P2/P3); (2) Enforce a 10% retry-ratio token bucket in official SDKs (`retry_tokens` refilled by successful responses); (3) Tag retried requests (`X-Retry-Attempt: 1`) so CoDel drops retries before fresh P0 attempts during overload.
explanation.deepDive: If a pod's CPU exceeds 85% parsing rejected traffic, push L4/XDP or Envoy edge rate-shedding rules upstream so P3 drops happen before full HTTP/JSON parsing.

codeExample.title: Priority-Aware Admission Controller with Gradient2 & Retry Budget
codeExample.code:
class PriorityGatewayLimiter:
    def __init__(self, initial_limit=50, min_limit=10, max_limit=200):
        self.limit = float(initial_limit)
        self.min_limit = min_limit
        self.max_limit = max_limit
        self.rtt_min = float('inf')
        self.in_flight = 0

    def admit(self, priority: int, is_retry: bool) -> bool:
        # Reserve 30% floor for P0; drop retries & P2/P3 first when near limit
        effective_cap = self.limit if priority == 0 else self.limit * (0.70 if priority >= 2 else 0.90)
        if is_retry and self.in_flight >= self.limit * 0.75:
            return False  # Protect fresh requests from retry storms
        if self.in_flight >= effective_cap:
            return False
        self.in_flight += 1
        return True

    def on_complete(self, rtt_ms: float):
        self.in_flight = max(0, self.in_flight - 1)
        self.rtt_min = min(self.rtt_min, rtt_ms)
        gradient = min(1.0, self.rtt_min / max(rtt_ms, 0.1))
        self.limit = max(self.min_limit, min(self.max_limit, self.limit * gradient + 1.0))

decisionFramework.problem: How to protect P0 checkout traffic and prevent retry storms during 3x spikes or 5x DB slowdowns.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a static global rate limit and blind client retries on 503.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Static rate limits can't adapt when DB latency rises 5x, and blind retries turn 3x spikes into 10x metastable outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Static global token bucket vs. Priority CoDel + Gradient2 + Retry Budgets.
decisionFramework.decision: Run per-pod Priority CoDel + Gradient2 concurrency limits, reserve a P0 floor, and enforce 10% SDK retry budgets + jittered Retry-After.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Requires maintaining route-to-priority mappings and SDK retry-budget discipline in exchange for autonomous overload survival.

decisionExercise.prompt: During a DB slowdown, your gateway sheds 40% of P2/P3 requests with `HTTP 503`, but gateway CPU jumps to 100% and P0 latency spikes anyway. Logs show `X-Retry-Attempt` on 70% of incoming traffic. What is missing?

options.label: Clients lack jittered `Retry-After` backoff and retry budgets, causing a retry storm; shed retried requests earlier and enforce a 10% SDK retry cap.
options.explanation: Correct! Unbounded client retries amplify overload; capping retries at ~10% of successful requests and dropping retries first breaks the metastable loop.

options.label: Increase the gateway's FIFO queue size from 1,000 to 100,000.
options.explanation: Larger queues worsen latency and memory pressure without reducing retry volume.

options.label: Promote P3 analytics requests to P0.

learningJourney.title: E & D · Evaluation, Assumptions, Limitations & Glossary
learningJourney.whyThisMatters: Documents traffic-mix assumptions, `RTT_min` drift traps, and core resilience terms.

explanation.foundation: This design assumes gateway pods are stateless per-request and that downstream services degrade gracefully when concurrency is capped.
explanation.core: Assumptions & Limitations: Sizing assumes 500K RPS normal / 1.5M RPS burst across 100 pods with P0/P1 <= 50% of total traffic. Because Gradient2 relies on `RTT_min` as its baseline, periodically decay or window `RTT_min` (e.g., reset every 5–10 minutes) so a topology change or cross-AZ shift doesn't permanently pin `RTT_min` to a stale value.
explanation.deepDive: Glossary: Goodput (requests completed successfully before client timeout); Metastable Failure (feedback loop where retries keep a system overloaded even after the initial spike ends); Gradient2 (Netflix's Little's Law adaptive concurrency limiter); Retry Budget (per-client cap on retry ratio, typically 10%).

knowledgeChecks.question: Why must the API gateway derive request criticality (`P0`–`P3`) from route + authenticated tenant metadata rather than a client-supplied header?

options.text: Untrusted clients or buggy SDKs would mark all traffic as `P0`, defeating priority isolation under overload.
options.feedback: Correct! Priority classification must be server-enforced at the edge.

options.text: HTTP headers cannot hold strings like `P0`.
options.feedback: HTTP headers hold arbitrary strings; the issue is trust and security.
Priority mapping is independent of header encoding.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Server-side route + tenant classification prevents priority inflation.

knowledgeChecks.question: By Little's Law (`L = lambda * W`), if 100 gateway pods normally serve 500K RPS at 10 ms service time (`L = 50`/pod) and DB latency jumps 5x to 50 ms, what happens without adaptive concurrency limits?

options.text: In-flight concurrency balloons 5x (or 15x during a 3x burst) to 25,000–75,000, exhausting DB connections and crashing workers.
options.feedback: Correct! Higher `W` multiplies in-flight `L` unless admission limits shrink and shed excess load.

options.text: In-flight concurrency drops to zero automatically.
options.feedback: Slower `W` increases `L` unless arrival rate `lambda` is shed.

options.text: DB latency automatically drops back to 10 ms.
TCP merges all 75,000 requests into one packet.
options.feedback: TCP does not merge separate HTTP requests.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Adaptive concurrency limits cap `L` to protect downstream pools when `W` spikes.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should `RTT_min` in a Gradient2 concurrency limiter be periodically decayed or windowed (e.g., every 5–10 minutes)?

options.text: So a permanent routing or cross-AZ latency shift doesn't leave `RTT_min` pinned to an unreachably low historical value, which would permanently under-admit traffic.
options.feedback: Correct! Windowing `RTT_min` lets the limiter recalibrate to baseline infrastructure shifts.

options.text: Because floating-point numbers overflow after 10 minutes.
options.feedback: Floats do not overflow from age.

options.text: To force all clients to reconnect.
options.feedback: Windowing `RTT_min` does not close TCP connections.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Stale `RTT_min` values cause persistent false-positive throttling after network topology changes.

beginner.summary: Protect critical APIs like checkout during traffic spikes by tagging requests P0–P3, shedding low-priority traffic first, and capping retries.
beginner.keyTakeaway: When an API gateway gets overloaded, drop low-priority background traffic and retries early so critical checkout requests stay fast.
beginner.byteSummary: By sorting requests into P0–P3 tiers, measuring queue wait times with CoDel, and returning 503 with Retry-After to P2/P3 traffic, critical P0 checkout flows stay at 100% goodput.

intermediate.summary: Combine per-tier CoDel queues, DRR scheduling, Gradient2 adaptive concurrency limits, and 10% client retry budgets to keep P0 p99 <15 ms.
intermediate.keyTakeaway: When designing a priority load-shedding gateway, pair CoDel sojourn queues with Gradient2 Little's Law limits and Retry-After budgets.
intermediate.byteSummary: Per-pod CoDel + Gradient2 detects downstream slowdowns locally with zero Redis hops, shedding P3/P2 and retries first while reserving a 30% P0 floor.

advanced.summary: Local per-pod DRR + CoDel priority scheduler, windowed Gradient2 concurrency control, 30% P0 floor, and upstream retry-storm shedding.
advanced.keyTakeaway: When defending 500K+ RPS gateways against metastable retry storms, enforce server-side priority tags, shed retries before fresh P0 attempts, and window RTT_min.
advanced.byteSummary: Combining server-derived P0–P3 DRR + CoDel queues, windowed Gradient2 `L = lambda * W` limits, and 10% retry budgets keeps P0 <15 ms p99 even under 5x DB slowdowns and 3x bursts.
